title: Triangular dihalide monolayers: ground states from budgeted energy mapping

decision_points.kind: evidence discovered in the structures plus a cross-check measurement
decision_points.fork: Are the six nearest neighbours equivalent in the rectangular cells of VBr2, VI2 and MnCl2?
decision_points.wrong_choice: Treat the 1.3-1.6 % split (4 + 2 bonds) as negligible and map one nearest-neighbour bond per ideal triangular shell
decision_points.consequence: The true exchanges differ by 40-70 % (12.3 vs 7.8, 4.0 vs 1.1, 1.2 vs 1.8 meV); the 120-degree state is predicted instead of the incommensurate spirals (VBr2, MnCl2) and the collinear stripe (VI2); prediction RMSE 0.43-5.6 meV/site

decision_points.kind: aliasing exposed only by a cross-check (budget pressure toward small cells)
decision_points.fork: Which supercell makes a four-state pair free of periodic images within the coupling range
decision_points.wrong_choice: A cell four lattice constants long for the 2a (third-neighbour) pair, so its image at -2a is the same coupling
decision_points.consequence: J3 doubled: Ni spirals off by 0.07-0.15 1/A; predictions off by 0.9-10.6 meV/site for Ni, VCl2, MnBr2, MnI2

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (exchange range) with a textbook confounder
decision_points.wrong_choice: Stop after J2 (MnBr2/MnI2 then sit in the J1-J2 stripe phase, J2/J1 > 1/8)
decision_points.consequence: Ni compounds become ferromagnets and MnBr2/MnI2 collinear stripes; the antiferromagnetic J3 actually stabilizes the 120-degree state in MnBr2/MnI2

decision_points.kind: model class for the ground-state search
decision_points.fork: Compare candidate commensurate states, or minimise over all wave vectors
decision_points.wrong_choice: Compare only FM, 120-degree and stripe energies (what a 6x6 lab cell can host)
decision_points.consequence: NiCl2/NiBr2 reported ferromagnetic, VBr2 a stripe, MnCl2 120-degree

decision_points.kind: discriminating experiment for a noise-level effect (anisotropy source)
decision_points.fork: How to find the VI2 moment direction
decision_points.wrong_choice: Compare stripe energies along x, y and z only, or take the single-ion easy axis
decision_points.consequence: Moment along c, 30.7 degrees from the true axis in the ac plane (tolerance 7 degrees); off-axis probes (x+z vs x-z) expose the tilt

decision_points.fork: How the nearest-neighbour tensor varies between the four bonds of the distorted cell
decision_points.wrong_choice: Copy the tensor measured on one bond to all four bonds
decision_points.consequence: Easy axis 39.9 degrees off (the staggered J_xy, J_yz parts do not cancel)

decision_points.kind: convention cascade from mapping to prediction
decision_points.fork: Pair counting when the mapped J are used to predict energies
decision_points.wrong_choice: Evaluate energies with every ordered pair counted while J came from a pair-once four-state formula

graded_fields: ground_states.<compound>.q_rlu within 0.02 1/A of any symmetry/translation equivalent of the reference
energy_predictions_meV_per_site: per-compound RMSE over its 3 configurations <= 0.3 meV/site
VI2_moment_direction within 7 degrees of the reference axis (sign-free)

length_estimate.catalog_value: unbounded (arbitrary configurations); mapping every bond class of all eight compounds in 36-site cells costs about 250-290 units
length_estimate.why: Eight compounds with structure inspection, supercell/aliasing design, collinear four-state mapping, Luttinger-Tisza on two lattice types with equivalence bookkeeping, an anisotropy experiment for VI2 and predictions in large cells.

runtime_dependencies: numpy (runtime image); the lab evaluates the teacher spin model, no extra dependencies

data_provenance.compounds_used: NiCl2 (PK 11815), NiBr2 (12821), VCl2 (16233), VBr2 (17997), VI2 (14160), MnCl2 (4157), MnBr2 (3579), MnI2 (2705); no Cr compound and no NiI2

notes: Teacher-model lab (the design's choice) built from the authors' archived AMaRaNTA parameters and validated against their archived four-state DFT energies (within-set residuals 0.003-0.03 meV, VI2 0.26 meV). Deviations from the design: (1) all eight compounds are graded (type + q) instead of three held-out ones; (2) the classical Monte Carlo ordering temperature and the Gamma-point magnon gap are not graded: with isotropic exchange there is no finite-T order in 2D, and the anisotropy that would set Tc or the gap (0.01-0.1 meV) is below the source's precision and logarithmically amplified, so Tc is not uniquely recoverable; finite-T physics is a rubric item; (3) the anisotropy fork is graded through the VI2 easy axis, which the off-diagonal exchange tilts 30.7 degrees from the single-ion axis; (4) energy predictions of unpurchasable configurations were added so that the exchange magnitudes (aliasing, pair counting) are graded where the ground state is insensitive. The 'sign convention' fork was dropped (the agent maps energies, so no sign is graded) and the 'spin normalization' fork is not graded (classical unit vectors throughout).

ablations.no_J3: ferromagnet for Ni, collinear stripe for MnBr2/MnI2
ablations.commensurate_only: ferromagnet for Ni, stripe for VBr2, 120-degree for MnCl2

prediction_rmse_meV_per_site.note: shared-reference four-state designs give a coherent error of ~0.08 meV/site (1 sigma) on the six-class distorted compounds, which sets the tolerance; the small J3 of the distorted compounds (0.07-0.17 meV) is deliberately not resolvable by this check

tightest_margins.predictions: VBr2 oracle RMSE 0.144 vs tolerance 0.3; nearest wrong path 0.43 meV/site (MnCl2, six equivalent NN)
tightest_margins.q: tolerance 0.02 1/A vs nearest wrong path 0.074 (NiBr2, J3 doubled); defensible spread <= 0.006
tightest_margins.VI2_axis: tolerance 7 deg vs 30.7 deg (Cartesian axes / SIA only); defensible spread <= 2.8 deg

risks: dev-easy: a careful agent grouping bonds by exact length, using alias-free cells and probing off-axis directions solves it with standard tools
teacher-model truth: VI2 tilt and anisotropies are below the source precision (0.1 meV); VI2 is reproduced worst by the model (0.26 meV rms within four-state sets)
NiBr2/NiCl2 assumed single-q spirals (anisotropic exchange <= 0.1 meV); not checked by Monte Carlo
